clue.text: Tough taking jewellery put in the pen

indicators.note: the jewellery is put in the pen, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
a ring is a piece of jewellery

explanation.surface: A hard case who took the jewels has been locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a prison or a writing tool here; it is a pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringy meat is fibrous and chewy, which is to say tough.

clue.text: A holy man goes on horseback or walks

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
a rider rides on horseback

explanation.surface: A saint either rides a horse or travels on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long steps, so the plural verb means walks with long paces.

clue.text: Stand out against insect repellent

parts.note: to stand out against something is to resist it
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An instruction to refuse insect repellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect repellent' reads as one product, but 'repellent' alone is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A resistant material keeps something out, so it is repellent in the sense of water-repellent.

clue.text: Many London shops display such material

indicators.note: the words Many London put the letters on show, like goods displayed in a shop window

explanation.surface: Lots of London stores have this fabric on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fabric, a material sold in shops.

clue.text: Plant which might become a worry

indicators.note: the letters of a worry could turn into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant that might grow into a problem for the gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering herb, a common wild plant.

clue.text: Support placed around wrongly-treated dog that's getting fatter

indicators.note: the support is put around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a pier is a pillar that supports a bridge

indicators.note: the dog is handled wrongly, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A badly fed dog is propped up because it is putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' could be a verb; it is a noun, a bridge pier. 'getting' is a link, leaving 'fatter' as the comparative definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Podgy means chubby, so the comparative podgier means plumper or fatter.

clue.text: There's no call to stamp, the appointment is salaried!

parts.note: a post is a job or appointment
a salaried worker is paid

explanation.surface: Cheerful news that a job is paid and no stamps are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp' looks like a foot movement; it is a postage stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent postpaid has its carriage already settled, so the sender need not affix a stamp.

clue.text: Cleaning block, squire?

parts.note: to deter is to block or discourage
a squire is a gentleman, or gent

explanation.surface: A squire wonders about a block of soap for cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent as an adjective describes something with a cleansing action.

clue.text: Little land is rented out

parts.note: a property let is rented out to a tenant

explanation.surface: A small plot of ground is leased.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, a little piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Remains — note back-up is expected

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: in a down clue going back up means the word is reads upwards

parts.note: something due is expected

explanation.surface: A memo warns that the remaining backup is on its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' looks like a reserve copy; split, it reverses 'is' to SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is what is left over, the remains of something.

clue.text: A neat sneak-thief

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is someone who steals cattle, not a tidy pickpocket

explanation.surface: A tidy pickpocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler steals livestock, a thief of cattle.

clue.text: Resolves to provide seating

definitions.meaning: to resolve a dispute is to settle it
a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

explanation.surface: Decides to put out some chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolves means sorts out a matter; old wooden benches are another sense, so both meet in one word.

clue.text: Paid no creditors? This could well be the outcome!

definitions.text: Paid no creditors? This could well be the outcome!

indicators.note: the result produced from the letters of paid no creditors, rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm that failed to pay its creditors may end up wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: rearranging the letters gives the likely fate of a company that pays nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that defaults on its debts may be dissolved as a legal corporation.

clue.text: Employees of the county

definitions.meaning: workers are the staff of a firm
The short form of Staffordshire, an English county in the Midlands

explanation.surface: The workers employed by a county council.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers as a body are staff, and Staffordshire, an English Midlands county, is abbreviated the same way.

clue.text: Star famed for converting country property

indicators.note: the letters of star famed are converted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A celebrity known for doing up a house in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converting' sounds like property renovation, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmstead is a farm with its buildings, a rural holding.

clue.text: A know-all's judicious measure

parts.note: a judicious person is wise
an acre is a measure of land area

explanation.surface: A smart alec's careful assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who pretends to great knowledge, a smart alec.

clue.text: Sound as if aching for a drink

indicators.note: the phrase is said out loud to give a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: a sham pain is pretend aching

explanation.surface: A fake ache put on to get a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine from France.

clue.text: Derision about sanctimonious love — it can sting

indicators.note: the derision is placed about the other pieces, around them

parts.note: scorn is derision or contempt
pi is slang for sanctimonious, short for pious
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Contempt for a pious romance can be hurtful.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion is an arachnid with a venomous stinging tail.

clue.text: Drop what may have a bad effect on the viewer

definitions.meaning: a sheer drop of water, a large waterfall

definitions.text: what may have a bad effect on the viewer
definitions.meaning: an eye condition clouding the lens, harmful to someone's sight

explanation.surface: A fall that could spoil the view for someone watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A great waterfall and a clouding of the eye lens that impairs vision share one name.

clue.text: Frightening split around large aeroplane's engine casing

indicators.note: the frightening word is split open and wrapped around the other piece

parts.note: cowing someone is frightening them into submission
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Something scary broke apart around a big plane's engine cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowling is the removable metal covering over an aircraft engine.

clue.text: A pastry's turned over in layers

indicators.note: the phrase a pastry's is turned over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pastry, and the possessive gives tart's

explanation.surface: A pastry flipped so its layers show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses ATARTS (A plus TART'S) as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, as in rock or society.

clue.text: Scratches ears. Bad mistake!

indicators.note: the letters of ears and bad are mistaken, placed in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Scratching one's ears is a terrible error.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or wear away a surface, so abrades means scratches.

clue.text: A service the non-drinker takes comfort in

indicators.note: the non-drinker takes the comfort inside, holding it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who does not drink alcohol
ease is comfort

explanation.surface: A teetotaller finds solace in a set of tableware.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is a matching service of cups, saucers and pot.

clue.text: Means to cope with driving rain

definitions.text: Means to cope with driving rain

parts.words: Means to cope with driving rain
parts.note: driving rain is rain hitting a car being driven, and this is the device on the front glass that sweeps it away

explanation.surface: A way to deal with rain blown hard by the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's blade on the front glass clears water so the driver can see.

clue.text: Mean with a woman

parts.note: the norm is the average or mean

explanation.surface: Being unkind to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like unkind; it is the statistical average.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's first name.

clue.text: A little mite, English, not coloured

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount, a mite

explanation.surface: A small English bug that has no colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mite' suggests a bug; here a mite and a whit both mean a very small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: White is the absence of hue, so a white thing is uncoloured.

clue.text: Arranging a rise, one pound, for a foreigner

indicators.note: the letters of a rise are being arranged in a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fixing a pay rise of a pound for an overseas worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' turns A RISE into ISRAE, then L and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli is a citizen of Israel, a foreigner from a British point of view.

clue.text: The skinhead bawled out when drunk

parts.note: the head of the word skin, its first letter
to wig someone is to scold them, so wigged means told off

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed thug shouted while he was intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' looks like a thug but means the head (first letter) of 'skin'; a wigging is an old British word for a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Swigged means gulped down, as a drink is drunk in large mouthfuls.

clue.text: Iris appears pleased with the fellow

parts.note: glad means pleased
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Iris looks happy to be with the man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, the gladdon or stinking iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladdon is the wild stinking iris, a plant of the iris family.

clue.text: A hero in the South-eastern American states

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A champion in the southeastern parts of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Greek legendary figure who slew the Minotaur.
